answer: To register a new identity, an attacker repeats this costly lock, and slashing burns it on proven duplicate behavior. Each agent must lock a stake behind an ivory-signed bond posted through a bridge contract that escrows funds across chains. Honest peers verify bonds from a public terrace of records, so forging hundreds of sybils means paying hundreds of stakes, making the attack economically irrational while genuine agents recover their stake on exit. From Agent0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
